title: Electricidad
blurb: De la ley de Ohm al cuadro eléctrico de tu pasillo.

lessons.title: Tensión, corriente y resistencia
lessons.summary: Las tres magnitudes que hay detrás de todo circuito y la ley que las une.

cards.title: La electricidad es carga en movimiento
cards.text:
Una corriente es un flujo de carga eléctrica. En un cable metálico son electrones que se empujan unos a otros. Cada electrón avanza despacio, pero el empuje recorre el cable casi al instante, como el agua en una manguera que ya está llena.

Por convenio, la corriente se dibuja fluyendo de + a −, en sentido contrario a los electrones. Todos los esquemas eléctricos usan este convenio.

deep.x: Electric current is a flow of electric charge. In metal wires, the charges that move are electrons, which are loosely bound to their atoms and can drift through the metal lattice.
Slow electrons, fast signal

Each electron drifts surprisingly slowly: in a household wire carrying a few amps, its average drift is well under a millimetre per second. But the "push" travels along the wire at a large fraction of the speed of light, because the wire is already full of electrons, like a hose already full of water.

items.l: how fast the signal travels in a cable

deep.x: Conventional current
Benjamin Franklin labelled charges "positive" and "negative" in the 1740s, before electrons were discovered in 1897. His guess about direction stuck.
Current is charge on the move; the push is fast even when the charges are slow.

cards.title: La analogía del agua
cards.text:
Imagina un depósito que alimenta una tubería.
• La tensión es la presión, que depende de la altura del agua.
• La corriente es cuánta agua pasa por segundo.
• La resistencia es un tramo estrecho de tubería que limita el caudal.

Más presión empuja más caudal; una tubería más estrecha deja pasar menos. Esa es toda la idea de la ley de Ohm.

deep.x: Electricity is invisible, so a water system makes a handy mental model. It isn't perfect, but it captures the key relationships.
What it explains well

x: A narrower pipe (more resistance) reduces flow
Flow is the same everywhere in a single pipe loop, just as current is the same everywhere in a series circuit

deep.x: Where it breaks down
An open switch doesn't spill electricity on the floor, and AC has no simple water equivalent.
Units
Voltage pushes, current flows, resistance restricts.

cards.title: La ley de Ohm
cards.text: La tensión (voltios, V) es igual a la corriente (amperios, A) por la resistencia (ohmios, Ω). Tapa en el triángulo la magnitud que buscas y las otras dos te dicen cómo obtenerla.
example: Batería de 12 V conectada a un calefactor de 4 Ω
cards.sketch: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g class="d"><path class="s" d="M110 20 L20 160 H200 Z"/><path class="s" d="M62 95L158 95"/><path class="s" d="M110 95L110 160"/></g><text class="" x="110" y="82" text-anchor="middle" style="font-size:34px">V</text><text class="" x="70" y="146" text-anchor="middle" style="font-size:34px">I</text><text class="" x="150" y="146" text-anchor="middle" style="font-size:34px">R</text><text class="a" x="268" y="62" text-anchor="middle" style="font-size:22px">V = I × R</text><text class="a" x="268" y="98" text-anchor="middle" style="font-size:22px">I = V ÷ R</text><text class="a" x="268" y="134" text-anchor="middle" style="font-size:22px">R = V ÷ I</text></svg>

deep.x: Georg Ohm published his law in 1827: in many materials, current is proportional to voltage. The ratio between them is the resistance.
The triangle
Worked examples

x: A 230 V kettle element of 24 Ω
A LED resistor: 5 V supply, 3 V LED, 20 mA wanted

deep.x: Where it doesn't apply

Ohm's law holds for metals and resistors at constant temperature. Diodes, LEDs and transistors are "non-ohmic": their current doesn't rise in proportion to voltage. A lamp filament's resistance also rises as it heats up.
Know any two of V, I and R, and you can find the third.

cards.title: Pruébalo: atenúa la bombilla
cards.text: Cambia la tensión y la resistencia. Observa la corriente y la potencia que la bombilla convierte en luz y calor.

deep.x: The simulator shows how voltage and resistance together set the current, and how the current turns into power in the bulb.

v.f: P = V × I = I² × R = V² ÷ R

deep.x: What to try

x: Double the voltage with the same resistance: current doubles and power quadruples
Double the resistance with the same voltage: current and power halve
Find the setting where the bulb glows brightly without "burning out"

deep.x: Why power rises so fast

v.unit: power in a 10 Ω bulb, W

deep.x: Power grows with the square of voltage, which is why a small overvoltage can quickly burn out a component.
Dimmers
Real dimmers don't add a resistor (that would waste energy as heat). They switch the power on and off very fast, or control LED drivers electronically.
Power rises with the square of voltage or current.

cards.title: Lo que hace daño es la corriente
cards.text:
Tu cuerpo también es una resistencia. Lo que importa para la seguridad es cuánta corriente lo atraviesa y por dónde.
Hacia 1 mA notas un cosquilleo. Cerca de 10 mA los músculos pueden agarrotarse y quizá no puedas soltarte. A partir de unos 50–100 mA a través del pecho, el corazón puede entrar en fibrilación.

Por eso los diferenciales de casa saltan a 30 mA: mucho antes de la zona peligrosa.

deep.x: The danger of electric shock depends on the current flowing through the body, its path and how long it lasts. Voltage matters because it drives that current through your body's resistance.

v.unit: effect of current through the body, mA (approx.)

deep.x: Your body's resistance

x: 230 V across wet hands, about 1,000 Ω

deep.x: Path and time

x: Hand to hand or hand to foot crosses the chest and heart
Longer exposure greatly increases harm, which is why speed of disconnection matters
Alternating current at 50 Hz is especially good at triggering heart fibrillation

deep.x: RCD protection
A 30 mA RCD must trip within 300 milliseconds at its rated current, and much faster at higher leakage. It limits both current and time.

deep.r: around 50 V AC can be dangerous in wet conditions; that's why bathrooms and pools use even lower "safety extra-low voltage"

cards.title: Conductores y aislantes
cards.text:
En los metales, algunos electrones pueden moverse libremente, así que la corriente fluye con facilidad: cobre, aluminio, plata. En los aislantes, como el plástico, el caucho, el vidrio y la madera seca, los electrones están muy sujetos y apenas circula corriente.

Los cables combinan ambos: un núcleo de cobre dentro de una funda de plástico.

deep.x: Materials differ enormously in how easily current flows through them. The difference comes from how tightly electrons are bound to atoms.
Best conductors
Why copper?

Silver conducts slightly better but costs far more. Copper is the best balance of conductivity, cost, flexibility and corrosion resistance. Aluminium is lighter and cheaper, so overhead power lines use it.
In between
Superconductors
Some materials, cooled to very low temperatures, conduct with zero resistance. MRI scanners use superconducting coils cooled by liquid helium.
Pure water is a poor conductor; the dissolved salts in real water make it dangerous.

cards.title: Resistencia de un cable
cards.text: La resistencia de un cable aumenta con su longitud y disminuye con su sección. Por eso los tendidos largos necesitan cables más gruesos, y por eso los alargadores finos se calientan.

deep.x: A wire's resistance depends on its material, length and cross-section. Longer wires resist more; thicker wires resist less.
Example

x: 50 m of 2.5 mm² copper (25 m there and back)

deep.x: At 16 A, that's a voltage drop of about 5.4 V, around 2% of 230 V.
Why it matters

x: Voltage drop: long runs deliver less voltage at the far end
Heat: current through resistance produces heat (P = I²R)
Wiring rules limit voltage drop, typically to a few percent

deep.x: Common sizes in homes
Warm extension leads
A thin, coiled extension lead powering a heater can overheat: high current, small cross-section, and a coil that traps the heat.
Long run or big load? Use a thicker cable.

cards.title: Medir con unidades
cards.text: Los prefijos mantienen los números manejables. Un cargador de móvil da unos 2 A, un sensor consume unos pocos miliamperios y la red de transporte lleva kilovoltios.

deep.x: Electrical quantities span huge ranges, from microamps in sensors to kiloamps in power stations. Metric prefixes keep numbers manageable.
Typical values
Real-world voltages

items.b: 5 V (up to 48 V with fast charging)

deep.x: Converting
Instruments
A multimeter measures volts, amps and ohms. Voltage is measured across a component; current is measured by putting the meter in the loop.
Mind the prefix: a milliamp and a megawatt are worlds apart.

cards.title: Cortocircuitos
cards.text: Un cortocircuito es un camino casi sin resistencia entre fase y neutro. Por la ley de Ohm, la corriente se vuelve enorme y calienta los cables en una fracción de segundo. Los fusibles y los magnetotérmicos existen para cortarla antes de que empiece un incendio.

deep.x: A short circuit creates a path with almost no resistance between conductors at different voltages. By Ohm's law, the current becomes enormous.
How big?
Home breakers are rated to safely interrupt fault currents of several thousand amps; the "6000" printed on many breakers means 6 kA.
Causes
Earth faults
A live wire touching a metal appliance case is an earth fault. With proper earthing, current flows to earth and the breaker or RCD trips, instead of the case becoming live.
Fuses and breakers exist to cut a short circuit before the cable becomes a heater.

cards.title: Circuitos abiertos y cerrados
cards.text: La corriente solo circula por un bucle completo. Un interruptor simplemente abre el bucle (apagado) o lo cierra (encendido). Un cable roto, un fusible fundido o un borne suelto abren el circuito.

deep.x: Current only flows around a complete loop from the source and back. Break the loop anywhere and the current stops everywhere in that loop.
Ways a circuit opens
Troubleshooting
When something doesn't work, check the loop step by step: supply, protection, switch, wiring, then the device.
Safety note
An open switch on the neutral side would leave a lamp holder live even when "off". That's why switches must break the live conductor.
No loop, no current.

quiz.q: Una pila de 9 V hace circular corriente por una resistencia de 450 Ω. ¿Cuál es la corriente?
quiz.explain: I = V ÷ R = 9 ÷ 450 = 0,02 A, es decir, 20 mA.

quiz.q: En la analogía del agua, ¿qué hace el papel de la tensión?
options: La rapidez con la que fluye el agua
La presión del agua (altura del depósito)
quiz.explain: La tensión es el empuje, como la presión. El caudal es la corriente; el estrechamiento de la tubería es la resistencia.

quiz.q: Duplicas la resistencia y mantienes la misma tensión. La corriente…
quiz.explain: I = V ÷ R. El doble de R con la misma V da la mitad de corriente.

quiz.q: ¿Por qué los tendidos de cable largos necesitan cables más gruesos?
options: La resistencia crece con la longitud, así que una sección mayor lo compensa
Los cables largos llevan menos tensión
quiz.explain: R = ρ × L ÷ A: más sección compensa más longitud.

quiz.q: ¿Qué hace un interruptor?
quiz.explain: Apagado = circuito abierto; encendido = circuito cerrado.

lessons.title: Circuitos en casa
lessons.summary: Serie frente a paralelo, potencia y lo que hacen de verdad los automáticos de tu cuadro.

cards.title: Serie frente a paralelo
cards.text:
En serie, los componentes comparten un único bucle. Por todos pasa la misma corriente y la tensión se reparte entre ellos. Un solo corte lo apaga todo, como las antiguas luces de Navidad.

En paralelo, cada componente tiene su propio camino hasta la alimentación. Cada uno recibe toda la tensión y se puede encender o apagar por separado.

deep.x: Components can be connected one after another (series) or side by side (parallel). Homes use parallel wiring, but both arrangements appear in electronics.
Resistances
Christmas lights
Old strings wired in series went completely dark when one bulb failed. Modern strings use shunts or parallel sections so one failure doesn't kill the rest.
Batteries

x: In series, voltages add: two 1.5 V cells give 3 V
In parallel, capacity adds at the same voltage

deep.x: Series shares voltage; parallel shares current.

cards.title: Tu casa está cableada en paralelo
cards.text:
Cada enchufe y cada luz están conectados entre los conductores de fase (L) y neutro (N). Por eso cada aparato recibe los 230 V completos, y por eso apagar el hervidor no apaga la nevera.

Cuantos más aparatos enchufas, más corriente total circula por la fase. Ese total es lo que vigilan los automáticos.

deep.x: Every socket and light in your home is connected in parallel between live and neutral, so each gets the full 230 V and works independently.
Colours of the wires
Total current adds

x: Kettle 9.6 A + toaster 4 A + microwave 5 A

deep.x: Ring and radial circuits
Portugal and most of Europe use radial circuits: each runs out from the board to its sockets. The UK commonly uses ring circuits, which loop back to the board, with fused plugs.
Parallel wiring lets each appliance work alone, but all share the supply.

cards.title: Potencia
cards.text: La potencia (vatios) es la rapidez con la que se usa la energía. Multiplica la tensión por la corriente. Despejando, I = P ÷ V te dice cuánta corriente consume un aparato.

deep.x: Power is the rate at which energy is converted, measured in watts. For electrical devices, it's voltage times current.
Typical appliances
Current drawn at 230 V
Heat appliances are hungry
Anything that heats (kettle, oven, heater, iron, hair dryer, water heater) draws large currents. Electronics draw little.
Watts vs volt-amps
For motors and some electronics, voltage and current aren't perfectly in step, so "apparent power" (VA) can be higher than real power (W). Contracted power in Portugal is in kVA for this reason.
Heating is power-hungry; electronics sip.

cards.title: Magnetotérmicos frente a diferenciales
cards.text:
Un magnetotérmico (PIA) protege el cable. Si circula demasiada corriente, el cable se sobrecalentaría, así que salta. Lo típico en un circuito de enchufes es uno de 16 A.

Un diferencial protege a las personas. Compara la corriente que sale por la fase con la que vuelve por el neutro. Si faltan unos 30 mA, se han fugado por algún sitio, quizá a través de una persona, y salta en una fracción de segundo.

deep.x: A home consumer unit has two kinds of protection that do different jobs: breakers protect cables, RCDs protect people.
How a breaker works

items.b: a bimetal strip bends with sustained overload
a coil reacts instantly to short circuits

deep.x: How an RCD works
It compares current on live and neutral. Normally they're equal. If 30 mA goes missing, it must be leaking somewhere, possibly through a person, so the RCD trips within a fraction of a second.
The test button

steps: Press T button monthly or as advised

deep.x: In Portugal
Portuguese rules require 30 mA residual current protection for socket circuits in homes. RCBOs combine breaker and RCD in one device.
Breakers save cables; RCDs save lives.

cards.title: Leer tu factura: kWh
cards.text: Pagas energía, no potencia. Energía = potencia × tiempo, y se mide en kilovatios hora (kWh). Un kWh es 1 kW funcionando durante una hora.
cards.sketch: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g class="d"><rect class="s" x="60" y="38" width="200" height="104" rx="8"/><rect class="s bgf" x="80" y="62" width="160" height="38" rx="3"/><circle class="a" cx="160" cy="122" r="6"/></g><text class="mono" x="160" y="89" text-anchor="middle" style="font-size:20px">0 1 2 4 6.8</text><text class="a" x="230" y="128" text-anchor="middle" style="font-size:18px">kWh</text><text class="" x="160" y="170" text-anchor="middle" style="font-size:17px">energía = potencia × tiempo</text></svg>

deep.x: You pay for energy, not power. Energy is power multiplied by time, measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh).
Examples

items.a: 150 W fridge average for a day

deep.x: What it costs
Your bill in Portugal
Time-of-use tariffs
Bi-hourly and tri-hourly tariffs ("bi-horário", "tri-horário") make night electricity cheaper. Running washing machines, dishwashers and EV charging at night saves money if you choose these tariffs.
Watts tell you how fast; kilowatt-hours tell you how much.

cards.title: Circuitos típicos de una casa
cards.text: En Portugal y en buena parte de Europa, las viviendas se dividen en circuitos, cada uno con su propio automático: alumbrado, enchufes generales, cocina y grandes aparatos como el horno o el termo.

deep.x: Homes are divided into several circuits, each with its own breaker, so a fault on one doesn't shut down the house and cables are sized for their load.
Why separate circuits

x: Each cable is sized for its breaker
A fault trips only one area
Heavy loads don't share with lights

deep.x: A typical Portuguese board
Labelling
Each breaker should be labelled. When work is needed, you know which one to switch off, and electricians work faster.
One circuit per job keeps faults local.

cards.title: Consumo en espera
cards.text: Muchos aparatos consumen aunque estén «apagados»: televisor, router, cargadores, cafetera. Cada uno puede gastar solo unos pocos vatios, pero funcionando todo el año, se acumula.

deep.x: Many devices keep drawing power when "off" or in standby: TVs, routers, chargers, set-top boxes, coffee machines. Individually small, together they add up.
Example
Typical standby draws
EU rules
EU ecodesign rules limit standby to 0.5 W for many products, with higher limits for networked devices that must stay connected.
Cutting it

x: Switchable power strips for TV and audio
Check settings like "quick start" that keep devices warm

deep.x: The cheapest kilowatt-hour is the one you don't waste in standby.

cards.title: Potencia contratada
cards.text: En Portugal contratas con tu comercializadora una potencia máxima, por ejemplo 6,9 kVA. Si enciendes demasiados aparatos a la vez, salta el interruptor general (ICP). Más potencia contratada implica un término fijo diario más alto.

deep.x: In Portugal, households contract a maximum power with their supplier. If total demand exceeds it, the supply is limited and the main breaker or meter cuts off.
Current available
The fixed charge
Higher contracted power means a higher fixed daily charge, whether you use it or not. Many households overpay by contracting more than they need.
Choosing

steps: List appliances used at the same time

x: Avoid running oven, dishwasher and heaters simultaneously to stay on a lower step
An EV charger or heat pump may require a higher level, or three-phase supply

deep.x: Contract for your real peak, not the sum of everything you own.

cards.title: ¿Saltará?
cards.text: Una potencia contratada de 6,9 kVA ≈ 30 A a 230 V. El horno (2 kW), el hervidor (2,2 kW) y la lavadora calentando agua (2 kW) suman 6,2 kW: cerca del límite. Añade un calefactor de 2 kW y salta el interruptor general.

deep.x: A worked example shows how quickly appliances add up to your contracted power.
Adding up

x: Under 6.9 kVA, close to the limit
Over the limit: the main breaker trips

deep.x: kVA vs kW
For heating appliances, kW and kVA are almost the same. For motors and electronics, the kVA can be a little higher than the kW.
Smart habits
Load managers can automatically pause an EV charger or water heater when other appliances push the total near the limit.
If the lights go out when the kettle goes on, look at what else is running.

cards.title: Clavijas y enchufes
cards.text: Portugal usa el enchufe tipo Schuko (tipo F), con contactos de tierra laterales. Reino Unido usa el tipo G, con tres patillas rectangulares y un fusible dentro de la clavija.

deep.x: Countries use different plug and socket designs, reflecting history, safety standards and voltage.
Common types in Europe

items.b: two pins, no earth, small devices
France, Belgium: earth pin in socket

deep.x: The UK's fused plug
Because UK ring circuits can be protected by 32 A breakers, each plug contains a fuse (usually 3 A or 13 A) to protect the appliance's thin flex.
Travel adapters

x: Adapters change the shape only, not the voltage
Most chargers accept 100–240 V and work worldwide
Heating appliances from 120 V countries can be damaged at 230 V

deep.x: There are around 15 main plug types in use worldwide, labelled A to N by the US International Trade Administration.

quiz.q: ¿Por qué cada enchufe de una casa recibe los 230 V completos?
options: Cada enchufe tiene su propio transformador
quiz.explain: En paralelo, cada carga está directamente entre fase y neutro, así que cada una recibe toda la tensión de la red.

quiz.q: Un calefactor de 1150 W funciona a 230 V. ¿Cuánta corriente consume?
¿Qué hace saltar un diferencial?
options: Una corriente total superior a su calibre
Que no toda la corriente que sale por la fase vuelve por el neutro
Que la tensión baje de 200 V
quiz.explain: Un diferencial mide el desequilibrio entre fase y neutro. La sobrecorriente es cosa del magnetotérmico.

quiz.q: Un horno de 1,5 kW funciona durante 4 horas. ¿Cuánta energía es?
quiz.explain: 1,5 kW × 4 h = 6 kWh.

quiz.q: Una potencia contratada de 6,9 kVA permite aproximadamente cuánta corriente a 230 V?
20 W en espera durante todo el año consumen unos…

lessons.title: CA y CC
lessons.summary: Por qué el enchufe alterna y la pila no.

cards.title: Corriente continua
cards.text: En CC, la corriente circula en un solo sentido con una tensión constante. Las pilas, los paneles solares y los cargadores USB dan CC, y todo circuito electrónico funciona con ella por dentro.

deep.x: Direct current (DC) flows in one direction at a steady voltage. It's what batteries, solar panels and USB chargers provide, and what all electronics use internally.
Sources of DC
Common DC voltages
Inside electronics
Chips need precise, steady DC, often 1–5 V. Power supplies convert mains AC to clean DC for them.
Electronics run on DC; the grid runs on AC.

cards.title: Corriente alterna

items.l: EE. UU. y parte de Brasil

cards.text: En CA, la tensión oscila entre positiva y negativa en una onda suave y cambia de sentido muchas veces por segundo. La red europea cambia 50 veces por segundo: 50 hercios.

deep.x: In alternating current (AC), the voltage rises and falls in a smooth wave, reversing direction many times a second.
One cycle
Why lights don't flicker visibly
Incandescent filaments stay hot between peaks. LED lamps need a good driver to avoid flicker at 100 Hz, which some people can perceive.
Hertz
The unit honours Heinrich Hertz, who demonstrated radio waves in the 1880s. One hertz means one cycle per second.
AC is a wave; 50 Hz means 50 full cycles every second.

cards.title: Por qué 230 V no es el pico
cards.text: La red se indica como 230 V, pero ese es el valor eficaz (RMS): la tensión continua que daría la misma potencia calorífica. Los picos reales llegan a unos 325 V.

deep.x: Mains voltage is quoted as an RMS (root mean square) value: the DC voltage that would produce the same heating effect. The actual peaks are higher.
The numbers
Why RMS?
RMS lets you use the same formulas as for DC. A 2,300 W heater on 230 V AC draws 10 A RMS and produces the same heat as on 230 V DC.
Practical consequences

x: Insulation and components must withstand the peaks, not just 230 V
"True RMS" meters measure correctly even when the waveform isn't a perfect sine

deep.x: Europe harmonised mains at 230 V in the late 1980s, bridging older 220 V and 240 V systems; tolerances allow roughly 207–253 V.

cards.title: La guerra de las corrientes

events.l: Central de CC de Edison en Nueva York
Patentes del motor de CA de Tesla
La CA ilumina la Exposición de Chicago
La CA del Niágara llega a Búfalo

cards.text: En la década de 1880, Edison defendía la CC; Westinghouse y Tesla apostaban por la CA. La CA ganó en las redes eléctricas porque los transformadores podían subir su tensión con facilidad para el transporte a larga distancia y bajarla para los hogares.

deep.x: In the 1880s and 1890s, Thomas Edison and George Westinghouse fought over which kind of current would power the world.
Edison's DC
Edison's DC systems worked well but had to be near customers: low-voltage DC couldn't travel far without big losses, so power stations were needed every mile or so.
Westinghouse and Tesla's AC
Westinghouse bought Nikola Tesla's AC motor patents. With transformers, AC could be sent at high voltage over long distances and stepped down for homes.
The fight
The outcome
Edison's company later merged into General Electric, which itself went on to build AC systems.

cards.title: ¿Por qué CA para la red?
cards.text: Las pérdidas en los cables dependen del cuadrado de la corriente. Los transformadores elevan la tensión para que la misma potencia circule con mucha menos corriente, y las pérdidas caen de forma drástica. Los transformadores solo funcionan con CA.

deep.x: Power losses in cables depend on the square of the current. Sending the same power at higher voltage means lower current and much smaller losses.
The effect of voltage
Ten times the voltage means a tenth of the current and a hundredth of the losses.
Transformers

A transformer uses two coils on an iron core. A changing current in one induces a voltage in the other, stepped up or down by the ratio of turns. It only works with changing current, which is why AC won.
In Portugal
REN operates the transmission grid at 150, 220 and 400 kV; distribution networks then step down to medium and low voltage.
High voltage for distance, low voltage for safety.

cards.title: Convertidores por todas partes
cards.text: El cargador de tu portátil convierte CA en CC (un rectificador más un regulador). Un inversor solar hace lo contrario: convierte la CC de los paneles en CA para la casa.

deep.x: Power electronics convert between AC and DC, and between voltages, everywhere around us.
Inside a charger
Why chargers got small
Switch-mode supplies run at tens or hundreds of kilohertz, so their transformers are tiny. New gallium nitride (GaN) chargers are even smaller and more efficient.
Other converters
Almost every device contains at least one converter.

cards.title: La CC vuelve
cards.text: La electrónica moderna convierte tensiones continuas con eficiencia, así que los enlaces submarinos y terrestres muy largos usan ahora corriente continua de alta tensión (HVDC). Los centros de datos y los VE también funcionan en gran parte con CC por dentro.

deep.x: Modern power electronics convert DC efficiently, so DC is returning for very long links, data centres, electric vehicles and solar systems.
HVDC
High-voltage DC lines have lower losses over very long distances and are the only practical option for long undersea cables, where AC suffers from cable capacitance.
Why DC suits long lines
Local DC
Homes with solar panels, batteries and EVs handle much of their energy as DC. Some designers propose DC microgrids to avoid repeated conversions.
DC lost the 1890s battle but is winning new ones.

cards.title: La frecuencia es compartida
cards.text: Todos los generadores de una red giran sincronizados. Si la demanda supera de repente a la oferta, la frecuencia baja ligeramente de 50 Hz, y los operadores deben añadir potencia en segundos para recuperarla.

deep.x: Every generator on a synchronous grid spins in lockstep. Grid frequency is a real-time measure of the balance between supply and demand.
Supply and demand
Continental Europe
Portugal and Spain are part of the continental European synchronous area, which stretches from Iberia to Turkey and Ukraine.
Inertia
Large spinning generators store energy that cushions sudden changes. Grids with lots of solar and wind need new sources of fast response, such as batteries and grid-forming inverters.
The 2025 Iberian blackout

On 28 April 2025, a cascade of generator disconnections linked to voltage problems left mainland Portugal and Spain without power for many hours. It highlighted the importance of grid stability services.
Frequency is the grid's heartbeat: it shows the balance every second.

cards.title: La onda senoidal
cards.text: Los generadores producen de forma natural una onda senoidal porque sus bobinas giran dentro de un campo magnético. Una vuelta completa de un generador de dos polos produce un ciclo; a 3000 rpm son 50 ciclos por segundo.

deep.x: Generators produce a sine wave naturally: as a coil rotates in a magnetic field, the induced voltage rises and falls smoothly with the angle.
Speed and poles
Why sine waves are useful

x: Transformers and motors work most efficiently with sine waves
Mathematics of sine waves makes calculations easier
Any periodic waveform can be built from sine waves (Fourier)

deep.x: Distortion

items: some electronics draw current in pulses

deep.x: Rotation in a magnetic field naturally makes a sine wave.

cards.title: Distintos países, distintas redes
cards.text: La mayor parte del mundo usa 220–240 V a 50 Hz. Norteamérica usa 120 V a 60 Hz, y Japón está dividido: 50 Hz en el este y 60 Hz en el oeste.

deep.x: Mains voltage and frequency vary between countries, a legacy of early choices that became too expensive to change.
Frequency
Japan's split
In the 1890s, Tokyo bought generators from Germany (50 Hz) while Osaka bought American ones (60 Hz). The two halves are still linked only through frequency converter stations.
For travellers

x: Check device labels: "100–240 V, 50/60 Hz" means it works anywhere
Clocks and some motors depending on frequency can run fast or slow
Hair dryers and kettles are usually single-voltage

deep.x: Read the label: most electronics are now universal.

quiz.q: ¿Qué significa 50 Hz?
options: La corriente cambia de sentido 50 veces por segundo (50 ciclos)
quiz.explain: Los hercios cuentan ciclos por segundo.

quiz.q: ¿Por qué ganó la CA en las redes eléctricas?
options: Los transformadores pueden subir y bajar su tensión fácilmente
quiz.explain: La alta tensión reduce las pérdidas en el transporte.

quiz.q: Un inversor solar convierte…
options: CC en CC de mayor tensión
quiz.explain: Los paneles producen CC; la casa usa CA.

lessons.title: Magnetismo y electroimanes
lessons.summary: Cómo la corriente crea campos magnéticos y viceversa.

cards.title: Campos magnéticos
cards.text: Un imán tiene un polo norte y un polo sur. Los polos opuestos se atraen; los iguales se repelen. La región invisible donde actúa es su campo magnético, que las limaduras de hierro hacen visible como líneas curvas.

deep.x: A magnet produces a magnetic field around it. Opposite poles attract and like poles repel. Field lines run from north to south outside the magnet.
Field lines
Iron filings sprinkled near a magnet line up along the field, showing curved lines that bunch together where the field is strongest, near the poles.
Units
Where magnetism comes from
Magnetism comes from moving charges and from the "spin" of electrons. In iron, nickel and cobalt, electron spins line up in regions called domains.
Cutting a magnet in half doesn't separate north and south: you get two smaller magnets, each with both poles.

cards.title: La Tierra es un imán

steps: Hierro fundido fluye en el núcleo

cards.text: El núcleo de hierro fundido de la Tierra crea un campo magnético. La aguja de una brújula es un pequeño imán que se alinea con él. El norte magnético se desplaza lentamente y no coincide exactamente con el polo norte geográfico.

deep.x: Earth's magnetic field is generated by moving molten iron in the outer core, acting like a giant dynamo. A compass needle lines up with this field.

steps: Liquid iron moves in outer core

deep.x: Magnetic vs geographic north
The magnetic north pole wanders. During the 20th century it drifted across northern Canada, and since the 1990s it has moved quickly towards Siberia, at tens of kilometres a year.
Declination

items.b: angle between magnetic and true north

deep.x: Field reversals
Protection
The magnetic field deflects much of the solar wind and cosmic radiation, helping protect the atmosphere and life.
Earth's core is a dynamo; your compass is reading it.

cards.title: La corriente crea un campo
cards.text: En 1820, Ørsted vio que la aguja de una brújula se movía cerca de un cable con corriente. Toda corriente crea un campo magnético que la rodea. Esto une la electricidad y el magnetismo.

deep.x: In 1820, Danish physicist Hans Christian Ørsted noticed that a compass needle moved when placed near a wire carrying current. It was the first proof that electricity and magnetism are linked.
The right-hand grip rule
Point your right thumb along the current; your curled fingers show the direction of the magnetic field circling the wire.
Field strength
Electromagnetism
James Clerk Maxwell later showed that electricity, magnetism and light are all aspects of one electromagnetic field, described by four equations.
Every current creates a magnetic field.

cards.title: Electroimanes
cards.text: Enrolla un cable en una bobina y los campos se suman. Pon un núcleo de hierro dentro y el campo se vuelve mucho más fuerte. Corta la corriente y el imán también se apaga.

deep.x: Coil a wire and the fields from each turn add up. Put an iron core inside and the field becomes hundreds or thousands of times stronger. Turn off the current, and the magnet turns off.
Strength
Soft vs hard iron
First electromagnet
William Sturgeon built the first electromagnet in 1824; Joseph Henry soon made much stronger ones by insulating wire and winding many turns.
An electromagnet is a magnet with an on/off switch.

cards.title: Dónde trabajan los electroimanes
cards.text: Los relés, las cerraduras eléctricas, los altavoces, los escáneres de resonancia magnética, las grúas de los desguaces y los contactores de tu cuadro eléctrico usan electroimanes.

deep.x: Electromagnets are hidden in countless everyday devices, wherever something must move, lock, sound or switch electrically.
Examples

items.b: current varies, cone moves, sound produced
coil closes heavy switch for motors

deep.x: Maglev trains
Maglev trains use powerful electromagnets to float above the track and propel themselves. Shanghai's airport maglev, opened in 2004, runs at up to about 300 km/h in regular service.
Wherever electricity makes something move, look for a coil.

cards.title: Relés
cards.text: Un relé usa una corriente pequeña por una bobina para cerrar un interruptor. Así, un microcontrolador de 3,3 V puede encender y apagar con seguridad un calefactor de 230 V.

deep.x: A relay is an electrically operated switch. A small current through a coil pulls a contact closed, switching a separate, often much larger circuit.
Why use a relay
Types
Protecting electronics
When the coil switches off, it produces a voltage spike. A diode across the coil (flyback diode) protects the transistor driving it.
Early computers such as the Harvard Mark I (1944) used thousands of relays to perform calculations.

cards.title: Inducción
cards.text: En 1831, Faraday descubrió lo contrario: un campo magnético variable empuja corriente por un cable cercano. Mete y saca un imán de una bobina y circula corriente. Así funcionan los generadores y los transformadores.

deep.x: In 1831, Michael Faraday discovered that a changing magnetic field induces a voltage in a nearby conductor. It's the principle behind generators, transformers and induction hobs.
Faraday's law

v.f: Induced voltage ∝ rate of change of magnetic flux

deep.x: Key point: change
A stationary magnet next to a coil induces nothing. Only changing fields induce voltage, which is why transformers need AC.
Applications
Lenz's law
The induced current opposes the change that caused it. Drop a magnet through a copper tube and it falls slowly, braked by its own induced currents.
Changing magnetism makes electricity.

cards.title: Placas de inducción
cards.text: Una placa de inducción hace pasar CA de alta frecuencia por una bobina bajo el vidrio. El campo variable induce corrientes directamente en la sartén de hierro, que se calienta. El vidrio se mantiene relativamente frío, y las sartenes no magnéticas no funcionan.

deep.x: An induction hob heats the pan directly. High-frequency current in a coil under the glass creates a rapidly changing magnetic field, which induces currents in the pan's base.
Efficiency
The pan test
If a magnet sticks firmly to the base, the pan works on induction. Cast iron and most stainless steel work; aluminium, copper and glass don't, unless they have a magnetic base layer.
Advantages
Safety
The hob only heats when a suitable pan is present, and the glass gets hot only from contact with the pan.
The hob doesn't heat; the pan heats itself.

cards.title: Carga inalámbrica
cards.text: Los cargadores de móvil usan la misma idea: una bobina en la base crea un campo variable y una bobina en el móvil lo capta. Es cómodo, pero menos eficiente que un cable, y necesita una buena alineación.

deep.x: Wireless chargers use induction: a coil in the pad creates a changing magnetic field, which induces current in a coil inside the phone.
The Qi standard
The Wireless Power Consortium's Qi standard is used by most phones. Qi2, introduced in 2023, adds magnets to align the phone and charger automatically.
Efficiency
Heat
Lost energy becomes heat, which is why phones warm up on pads. Heat is bad for battery life, so chargers slow down when the phone gets warm.
Other uses
Wireless charging trades some efficiency for convenience.

cards.title: Almacenamiento magnético
cards.text: Los discos duros guardan los bits como regiones diminutas imantadas en un sentido u otro. Las bandas de las tarjetas de crédito y las antiguas cintas de casete usan el mismo principio.

deep.x: Magnetic storage records information by magnetising tiny regions of a material in one direction or the other, representing ones and zeros.

items.b: tiny magnetic grains on spinning platters

deep.x: Hard drives today
Tape is still alive
Magnetic tape remains one of the cheapest and most durable ways to archive huge amounts of data. Large cloud providers still use tape libraries for backups.
Keep magnets away?
Strong magnets can erase card stripes and damage old tapes. Modern hard drives are well shielded from everyday magnets, and SSDs and chip cards don't use magnetic storage.
Every bit on a hard drive is a tiny magnet pointing one way or the other.

quiz.q: ¿Qué descubrió Ørsted en 1820?
options: Que una corriente eléctrica crea un campo magnético
quiz.explain: La aguja de una brújula se movió cerca de una corriente.

quiz.q: ¿Por qué una sartén de aluminio no funciona en una placa de inducción?
options: No es lo bastante magnética para que el campo la caliente con eficiencia
quiz.explain: La inducción necesita una base ferromagnética.

quiz.q: Un relé permite que una corriente pequeña…
quiz.explain: La bobina atrae y cierra un contacto independiente.

lessons.title: Motores y generadores
lessons.summary: Convertir electricidad en movimiento, y al revés.

cards.title: El efecto motor
cards.text: Un cable con corriente dentro de un campo magnético sufre una fuerza. Dobla el cable en forma de espira sobre un eje y las fuerzas en cada lado empujan en sentidos opuestos: gira.

deep.x: A wire carrying current inside a magnetic field feels a force at right angles to both. Bend the wire into a loop on an axle and the forces turn it.

items.m: length of wire in the field

deep.x: From force to rotation

steps: One side pushed up, other side down

deep.x: Direction
Fleming's left-hand rule: thumb for motion, first finger for field, second finger for current, all at right angles.
History
Michael Faraday demonstrated the first electric motor in 1821: a wire rotating around a magnet in a cup of mercury.
Stronger motors
Current plus magnetic field equals force.

cards.title: Motores de CC
cards.text: Los motores de CC pequeños usan un conmutador, un anillo partido que invierte la corriente cada media vuelta para que la bobina siga girando en el mismo sentido. Las escobillas rozan sobre él, lo que provoca desgaste.

deep.x: Simple DC motors use a commutator, a split ring that reverses the current in the coil every half turn, so it keeps spinning the same way.
Where they're used

items.b: cheap toys, car windows, small tools
drones, computer fans, cordless tools, EVs

deep.x: Speed control
The speed of a DC motor rises with voltage. Electronic controllers vary the average voltage by switching very fast (pulse-width modulation).
Brush wear
Brushes are carbon blocks that rub against the commutator. They spark, wear down and create electrical noise, which is why brushless designs have taken over in quality products.
Brushless motors replaced brushes with electronics.

cards.title: Generadores
cards.text: Un generador es un motor al revés: haz girar una bobina en un campo magnético (o un imán dentro de bobinas) y se induce una tensión. Las turbinas movidas por vapor, agua o viento hacen girar generadores que producen casi toda nuestra electricidad.

deep.x: A generator is a motor in reverse: turn a coil in a magnetic field, or a magnet inside coils, and a voltage is induced.
Prime movers
Big machines
Solar is different
Solar panels are the main exception: they produce electricity directly from light, with no moving parts or generator.
Bicycle dynamos
A bicycle dynamo is a tiny generator: the wheel spins a magnet inside a coil, lighting the lamp.
Almost all our electricity comes from something spinning a magnet.

cards.title: Motores de inducción
cards.text: La mayoría de los motores industriales, bombas y ventiladores son motores de inducción de CA. El estátor crea un campo magnético giratorio que induce corrientes en el rotor, y este persigue al campo. Simples, robustos y sin escobillas.

deep.x: The AC induction motor is the workhorse of industry. It has no brushes and a simple, tough rotor, and it starts directly from the mains.
Slip
The rotor always turns slightly slower than the rotating field, typically 2–5% slower. That difference, called slip, is what induces current in the rotor.
Inventors
Galileo Ferraris and Nikola Tesla independently developed induction motors in the late 1880s. Tesla's patents were bought by Westinghouse.
Squirrel cage

items: copper or aluminium bars shorted at both ends

deep.x: Spin a magnetic field and the rotor chases it.

cards.title: Los motores consumen mucha electricidad

items.l: de la electricidad mundial va a motores (estimación AIE)

cards.text: Los motores eléctricos suponen aproximadamente el 40–45 % del consumo eléctrico mundial, según la AIE, sobre todo en la industria: bombas, compresores y ventiladores. Motores más eficientes y el control de velocidad ahorran enormes cantidades de energía.

deep.x: Electric motors are everywhere in industry and buildings. According to the International Energy Agency, motor-driven systems use roughly 40–45% of the world's electricity.

items.l: of global electricity used by motors

deep.x: Where it goes
Saving potential
Upgrading to high-efficiency motors and adding speed control can cut motor energy use by 20–30% in many systems.
EU rules
Since 2021, EU ecodesign rules require most new industrial motors to meet efficiency class IE3, with IE4 required for many mid-sized motors since 2023.
Efficient motors are one of the biggest, least visible energy savings.

cards.title: Variadores de velocidad
cards.text: Un variador de frecuencia (VFD) cambia la frecuencia que recibe un motor de CA para controlar su velocidad. Como la potencia de ventiladores y bombas cae mucho con la velocidad, funcionar al 80 % de velocidad puede consumir solo cerca de la mitad de potencia.

deep.x: A variable frequency drive (VFD) controls an AC motor's speed by changing the frequency of the power it supplies. It saves energy wherever full speed isn't needed.

items.m: halving speed cuts power to an eighth

deep.x: The cube law

v.unit: power needed by a fan, % of full

deep.x: Without a drive
Traditionally, flow was reduced with valves or dampers while the motor ran at full speed: like driving with the brake on.
Other benefits
Where they're used
HVAC fans, water pumps, compressors, conveyors, elevators and electric vehicles all use variable speed drives.
Slowing a fan by 20% roughly halves its power.

cards.title: Motores de VE
cards.text: Los coches eléctricos usan motores de imanes permanentes o de inducción, a menudo con más del 90 % de eficiencia, frente a aproximadamente el 20–35 % de los motores de gasolina. Dan el par máximo desde parado.

deep.x: Electric vehicles use compact, highly efficient motors, usually permanent-magnet synchronous motors or induction motors.

v.unit: efficiency from energy source to wheels, % (approx.)

deep.x: Torque from standstill
Electric motors deliver maximum torque from zero speed, giving instant acceleration without a gearbox. Most EVs use a single fixed gear.
Motor types

items: slightly less efficient at low load

deep.x: Rare earths
Permanent magnets often contain neodymium and dysprosium, mostly processed in China. Manufacturers are developing motors that reduce or avoid rare earths.
Most of an EV's energy goes to the wheels, not to heat.

cards.title: Frenado regenerativo

steps: Acelerar: la batería mueve el motor
Energía de vuelta a la batería

cards.text: Cuando un VE frena, su motor funciona como generador y convierte el movimiento de nuevo en electricidad para recargar la batería. Por eso la conducción con un solo pedal aumenta la autonomía en ciudad.

deep.x: When an EV or hybrid slows down, its motor acts as a generator, turning the car's kinetic energy back into electricity to recharge the battery.
How much it recovers
In stop-and-go city traffic, regenerative braking can recover a substantial share of the energy used for acceleration, noticeably extending range. On motorways, with little braking, it helps less.
One-pedal driving

items.b: for hard stops and final hold

deep.x: Limits

items: Emergency braking still uses friction brakes

deep.x: Trains and lifts
Electric trains and some lifts also regenerate energy, feeding it back to the grid or to other trains.
Braking that charges the battery instead of heating the discs.

cards.title: Motores paso a paso y servos
cards.text: Los motores paso a paso se mueven en pasos exactos (impresoras 3D, CNC). Los servos usan realimentación para mantener un ángulo preciso (brazos robóticos, aviones RC). Ambos dan un movimiento que puedes controlar con precisión.

deep.x: Stepper motors and servos are designed for precise positioning rather than continuous power.
Stepper motors
Servos
A servo combines a motor, gearbox, position sensor and controller. It compares actual position with the target and corrects continuously.
Hobby servos
Small hobby servos take a pulse every 20 ms; the pulse width (about 1–2 ms) sets the angle. They're used in robotics kits and Arduino projects.
Steppers count; servos check.

cards.title: Placas de características
cards.text: Todo motor tiene una placa de características: potencia nominal (kW), tensión, corriente, velocidad (rpm) y clase de eficiencia (IE1 a IE5). Te dice qué alimentación y qué protección necesita.

deep.x: Every motor carries a nameplate listing the information needed to install, protect and run it correctly.
Efficiency classes

v.unit: efficiency of a typical 11 kW motor, % (approx.)

deep.x: Other nameplate data
Star and delta
Many three-phase motors can be connected in star or delta, which is why nameplates show two voltages: 230 V in delta or 400 V in star.
The nameplate tells you the supply, protection and efficiency the motor needs.

quiz.q: Un generador es básicamente…
quiz.explain: Al hacerlo girar se induce una tensión.

quiz.q: ¿Por qué los variadores de velocidad ahorran tanta energía en los ventiladores?
options: La potencia del ventilador baja aproximadamente con el cubo de la velocidad
quiz.explain: Un pequeño recorte de velocidad da un gran recorte de potencia.

quiz.q: El frenado regenerativo…
options: Aprieta más las pastillas de freno
Convierte el motor en generador para recargar la batería
quiz.explain: La energía cinética se convierte en electricidad.

lessons.title: La red eléctrica
lessons.summary: De la central a tu enchufe.

cards.title: Generación, transporte, distribución
cards.text: La electricidad se genera en centrales y en parques eólicos o solares, se lleva a grandes distancias por líneas de transporte de alta tensión y luego se distribuye a tensiones más bajas a pueblos, ciudades y hogares.

deep.x: The power grid has three main stages: making electricity, moving it long distances at high voltage, and distributing it locally at lower voltages.

steps: Power stations and wind or solar farms

deep.x: Voltage levels in Portugal
Who does what
Losses
Transmission and distribution losses in European grids are typically several percent of electricity generated, mostly in the lower-voltage distribution networks.
Electricity is made far away, moved fast at high voltage and delivered gently at low voltage.

cards.title: Transformadores
cards.text: Un transformador tiene dos bobinas alrededor de un núcleo de hierro. La CA en la primera bobina crea un campo variable que induce tensión en la segunda. La relación de espiras fija la relación de tensiones.

deep.x: A transformer changes AC voltage using two coils wound on an iron core. The ratio of turns sets the ratio of voltages.
Example
Energy conserved
Power in ≈ power out: big transformers are over 99% efficient.
Where you see them
The hum
The 100 Hz hum near transformers comes from the iron core changing size slightly with each magnetic cycle, an effect called magnetostriction.
Transformers trade voltage for current, almost without loss.

cards.title: ¿Por qué alta tensión?
example: 10 MW a 10 kV frente a 400 kV
cards.text: Las pérdidas en el cable son I² × R. Duplicar la tensión reduce a la mitad la corriente para la misma potencia y deja las pérdidas en una cuarta parte.

deep.x: Line losses depend on the square of the current. Raising the voltage lowers the current for the same power, slashing losses.
Doubling voltage

v.unit: relative losses for the same power, %

deep.x: Doubling voltage halves the current and cuts losses to a quarter.
Trade-offs

x: Higher voltages need taller towers and bigger insulators
Wider clearances to the ground and buildings

deep.x: Typical choices
High voltage carries power far; transformers make it safe at home.

cards.title: Equilibrar oferta y demanda
cards.text: La electricidad es difícil de almacenar a gran escala, así que la oferta debe igualar a la demanda en cada segundo. Los operadores de la red prevén la demanda y despachan centrales, importaciones, almacenamiento y respuesta de la demanda para mantener el equilibrio.

deep.x: Electricity must be produced at the same moment it's consumed. Grid operators balance supply and demand continuously, second by second.
Tools for balance
Reserves

items.b: replaces earlier reserves over longer periods

deep.x: Forecasting
Operators forecast demand using weather, calendars and past patterns, and forecast wind and solar output from weather models. Errors are covered by reserves.
Demand response
Large consumers, and increasingly households with smart devices, can reduce or shift use when the grid is stressed, often for payment.
The grid is a balancing act that never stops.

cards.title: La curva de demanda diaria
cards.text: La demanda es baja de noche, sube por la mañana y alcanza el máximo por la tarde-noche, cuando la gente cocina y calienta su casa. La producción solar llega a su pico a mediodía, lo que está cambiando las horas en que la electricidad es más barata.

deep.x: Electricity demand follows daily rhythms. Solar power has changed when electricity is cheapest, shifting cheap hours to midday.
The duck curve
The shape of net demand (demand minus solar) looks like a duck, first described in California around 2013.
What it means for prices

x: Midday prices can fall very low, even negative, on sunny days
Batteries charge at midday and discharge in the evening

deep.x: For homes

items: Run appliances at midday with solar

deep.x: The cheapest electricity is moving from night to midday.

cards.title: El mix renovable de Portugal

viz.unit: % de la electricidad portuguesa (aprox., año reciente)

cards.text: Las renovables (hidráulica, eólica, solar y biomasa) aportan la mayor parte de la electricidad de Portugal en un año típico, aproximadamente un 60–70 % en los últimos años según la lluvia y el viento. En 2016, el país funcionó cuatro días seguidos solo con renovables.

deep.x: Portugal is one of Europe's renewable leaders. Hydro and wind provide most renewable electricity, and solar is growing fastest.
Main sources
Year-to-year swings
Hydro output depends strongly on rainfall. In dry years, gas and imports fill the gap; in wet, windy years, renewables can exceed 70%.
Milestones

events.l: Sines and Pego coal plants close

deep.x: Challenges

x: Storage and flexibility for low-wind, low-rain periods
Grid connections for new solar and wind
Limited interconnection with the rest of Europe

deep.x: In Portugal, rain and wind largely decide the electricity mix.

cards.title: Interconexiones
cards.text: La red de Portugal está conectada con la de España, y la de España con la de Francia. Las interconexiones permiten a los países compartir excedentes eólicos o solares, pero los enlaces de la península ibérica con el resto de Europa son relativamente limitados.

deep.x: Interconnections link national grids so countries can trade electricity, share reserves and absorb surpluses. Portugal connects to Spain; Spain connects to France and Morocco.
The "energy island"

items.l: Spain–France interconnection vs Spain's generating capacity

deep.x: The Iberian Peninsula is often called an "energy island" because its links to France are small relative to its size.
Benefits
Iberian market
Portugal and Spain share a single wholesale electricity market, MIBEL, with prices set by the OMIE exchange. Prices are often identical in both countries.
More connections mean a more resilient, cheaper grid.

cards.title: El apagón de abril de 2025

events.l: problemas repentinos de tensión y frecuencia
el suministro vuelve poco a poco

cards.text: El 28 de abril de 2025, una pérdida repentina de generación desencadenó una cascada que dejó sin luz casi toda la España peninsular y Portugal continental durante muchas horas. Reponer una red desde cero («arranque autónomo») es lento y delicado.

deep.x: On 28 April 2025, shortly after 12:30 in Spain (11:30 in Portugal), a cascade of disconnections left almost all of mainland Spain and Portugal without power, in one of Europe's largest blackouts in decades.
What happened
Investigations pointed to voltage control problems: rising voltages caused generators to disconnect in sequence, and the grid lost synchronism with France within seconds.
Black start

steps: Plants with black-start ability start without grid

deep.x: In Portugal, hydro and gas plants able to start without external power were used to rebuild the grid.
Effects
A modern society runs on electricity; restoring it from zero takes hours.

cards.title: Almacenamiento en la red
cards.text: El bombeo hidráulico almacena energía subiendo agua cuando la electricidad es barata y soltándola por turbinas cuando se necesita. Las grandes baterías responden ahora en milisegundos para estabilizar la frecuencia.

deep.x: Storage lets grids save surplus energy for later. Pumped hydro has dominated for decades; batteries are now growing rapidly.
Pumped hydro in Portugal
Portugal has several pumped-storage plants, including Alqueva and the Tâmega system, whose Gouvães plant came online in the early 2020s with about 880 MW.
Round-trip efficiency
Other options
Pumped hydro still provides the large majority of the world's grid energy storage capacity.

cards.title: Redes inteligentes
cards.text: Los contadores inteligentes, los sensores y la automatización permiten a la red ver en tiempo real por dónde fluye la energía, integrar la solar en tejados y los VE, y desviar el flujo automáticamente alrededor de las averías.

deep.x: A smart grid uses sensors, communication and automation to monitor and control electricity flows in real time, integrating rooftop solar, batteries and EVs.
Smart meters
Most Portuguese homes now have smart meters that read consumption remotely, enable time-of-use tariffs and let the distributor change contracted power without visits.
Self-healing networks
Two-way flows
Privacy and security
Detailed consumption data can reveal household habits, so it's protected under GDPR. Grid automation also needs strong cybersecurity.
A smart grid sees, decides and reacts in real time.

quiz.q: ¿Por qué se transporta la electricidad a muy alta tensión?
options: Hace falta menos corriente, así que las pérdidas en los cables son mucho menores
quiz.explain: Las pérdidas crecen con el cuadrado de la corriente.

quiz.q: Un transformador funciona porque…
options: Un campo magnético variable induce una tensión en la segunda bobina
quiz.explain: Se basa en la inducción con CA.

quiz.q: El almacenamiento por bombeo…
options: Bombea agua cuesta arriba cuando la electricidad es barata y genera después
quiz.explain: Almacena energía en forma de altura.

lessons.title: Baterías
lessons.summary: Química, capacidad y cómo hacer que duren.

cards.title: Cómo funciona una batería

steps: Los electrones pasan por tu aparato

cards.text: Una batería tiene dos electrodos separados por un electrolito. Una reacción química expulsa electrones de un electrodo, los hace pasar por tu circuito y los devuelve al otro. Al recargar, la reacción se invierte.

deep.x: A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy. Two electrodes with different chemical potential are separated by an electrolyte that lets ions move but not electrons.

steps: Chemical reaction at anode releases electrons

deep.x: In a lithium-ion cell

items.b: lithium ions move from anode (graphite) to cathode
charger pushes them back to the anode
thin porous film keeping electrodes apart

deep.x: History
Primary vs secondary
A battery is a controlled chemical reaction that pushes electrons through your circuit.

cards.title: Capacidad: Ah y Wh
cards.text: Los amperios hora (Ah) indican cuánta carga guarda una batería. Multiplica por la tensión para obtener la energía en vatios hora (Wh), que es lo que de verdad importa para comparar baterías.

deep.x: Battery capacity is quoted in amp-hours (Ah) or milliamp-hours (mAh), but energy in watt-hours (Wh) is the fair way to compare batteries of different voltages.
Examples
Power banks
A 10,000 mAh power bank stores about 37 Wh at 3.7 V. After conversion losses, it can deliver roughly 60–70% of that to a phone.
Airline rules
Airlines generally allow power banks up to 100 Wh in cabin baggage without approval, and between 100 and 160 Wh with airline approval. They're banned from checked bags.
Compare batteries in watt-hours, not milliamp-hours.

cards.title: Químicas de batería
cards.text: El plomo-ácido es barato y pesado (baterías de arranque de coche). El ion-litio almacena mucha más energía por kilo (móviles, portátiles, VE). El LFP, una variante de litio-ferrofosfato, sacrifica un poco de densidad energética a cambio de seguridad y larga vida.

deep.x: Different battery chemistries trade energy density, cost, safety and lifespan.
Common types

items.b: safe, long-life, storage and many EVs

deep.x: LFP's rise
Lithium iron phosphate cells contain no cobalt or nickel, are cheaper and tolerate more cycles. They now power a large share of EVs, especially in China, and most home batteries.
New chemistries
The best chemistry depends on whether you need energy, cost, safety or life.

cards.title: Tasa C
cards.text: La tasa C compara la corriente de carga o descarga con la capacidad. A 1C una batería se carga o se vacía por completo en una hora aproximadamente; a 0,5C, en dos horas; a 3C, en 20 minutos. Las tasas C altas generan calor y desgaste.

deep.x: The C-rate expresses charge or discharge current relative to capacity. It shows how hard a battery is being worked.
Examples

x: about 1 hour to charge or discharge

deep.x: Why it matters
Charging curve
Fast charging slows down above about 80%, because the cell's voltage rises and the charger reduces current to protect it. That's why EV charging stops are often 10–80%.
High C-rates are fast but hard on batteries.

cards.title: Estado de carga y ciclos
cards.text: Las baterías de litio duran más si no pasan mucho tiempo al 0 % ni al 100 %. Muchos VE recomiendan cargar al 80 % para el uso diario y al 100 % solo antes de viajes largos.

deep.x: Lithium-ion batteries age faster when kept at very high or very low charge for long periods, especially when warm.
Practical advice

x: For daily use, charging to about 80% extends life
Charge to 100% before long trips, then drive soon after
Avoid leaving devices fully charged in hot cars or sun

deep.x: Phone features
Many phones offer "optimised charging", pausing at 80% overnight and finishing just before you wake.
LFP is different
LFP batteries tolerate 100% charge better, and some manufacturers recommend charging them fully regularly so the battery management system can calibrate.
Middle charge, moderate temperature: that's where lithium is happiest.

cards.title: Por qué envejecen las baterías
cards.text: Cada ciclo provoca pequeños cambios químicos que reducen poco a poco la capacidad. El calor lo acelera mucho. Los niveles de carga altos y la carga muy rápida también añaden estrés.

deep.x: Every charge and discharge causes tiny, irreversible chemical changes that slowly reduce capacity and increase internal resistance.
Main stress factors
Calendar vs cycle ageing

items: worse with deep cycles and fast charging

deep.x: End of life
A battery is usually considered "worn out" at 70–80% of original capacity. EV batteries at that point can find a second life in stationary storage.
Heat is a battery's worst enemy.

cards.title: Vida en ciclos
cards.text: Las celdas LFP suelen aguantar varios miles de ciclos completos antes de bajar al 80 % de capacidad, por eso son populares para el almacenamiento doméstico. Las NMC típicas aguantan menos, pero almacenan más energía por kilo.

deep.x: Cycle life is the number of full charge-discharge cycles before capacity falls to a threshold, often 80%.
What it means for EVs
Partial cycles
Two charges from 50% to 100% count roughly as one full cycle. Shallow cycles are gentler than deep ones.
Real-world data
Studies of real EV fleets show many batteries keep around 90% of capacity after 100,000–200,000 km, better than many early predictions.
For home storage cycling every day, LFP's long life is a big advantage.

cards.title: Sistemas de gestión de baterías
cards.text: Un BMS vigila la tensión y la temperatura de cada celda, las equilibra, limita la corriente y desconecta el paquete si algo va mal. Un paquete de litio nunca debe usarse sin uno.

deep.x: A battery management system (BMS) monitors and protects every cell in a lithium pack. Large lithium packs should never run without one.
Cell balancing
Cells in a pack drift apart slightly. The BMS balances them so no cell is overcharged or over-discharged while others are still mid-range.
State of charge
The BMS estimates remaining charge from voltage, current and temperature. That's the percentage on your phone or EV dashboard.
Protection
The BMS is the battery's brain and bodyguard.

cards.title: Fuga térmica
cards.text: Si una celda de litio se daña, se sobrecarga o se sobrecalienta, puede iniciar una reacción que se calienta sola y se extiende a las celdas vecinas. Estos incendios son difíciles de apagar y pueden reavivarse.

deep.x: Thermal runaway is a self-heating chain reaction in a lithium cell. Once started, it releases heat and flammable gases and can spread to neighbouring cells.
Causes
Why fires are hard
Burning cells produce their own oxygen from the cathode, so smothering doesn't work well. EV fires need large amounts of water for cooling and can reignite hours or days later.
LFP is safer
Warning signs
A swollen battery is a warning: stop using it and dispose of it safely.

cards.title: Paquetes en serie y en paralelo
cards.text: Las celdas en serie suman tensión; las celdas en paralelo suman capacidad. Un paquete de VE puede combinar unos 100 grupos en serie para llegar a unos 400 V.

deep.x: Battery packs combine cells in series to raise voltage and in parallel to raise capacity and current.
Notation

items.b: four cells in series, about 14.8 V

deep.x: EV voltages
Most EVs use around 400 V packs. Some newer cars use 800 V architectures, allowing faster charging with lower current and thinner cables.
Weakest link
In series, the weakest cell limits the whole string, which is why matched cells and good balancing matter.
Series for voltage, parallel for capacity.

quiz.q: Una batería de 12 V y 50 Ah almacena unos…
Cargar a 0,5C tarda aproximadamente…
¿Qué acelera más el envejecimiento de una batería?
options: El calor y pasar mucho tiempo al 100 %
quiz.explain: El calor y los estados de carga altos añaden estrés.

lessons.title: Energía solar
lessons.summary: Cómo los paneles convierten la luz del sol en electricidad.

cards.title: El efecto fotovoltaico

steps: La luz incide en el silicio
La unión los empuja en un sentido

cards.text: Una célula solar es una fina lámina de silicio con dos capas tratadas de forma distinta. La luz libera electrones, y la unión entre las capas los empuja en un sentido: una corriente continua.

deep.x: A solar cell turns light directly into electricity. Photons knock electrons loose in silicon, and a built-in electric field at the junction pushes them in one direction.
The junction

items.b: built-in field pushes electrons one way

deep.x: History

events.l: Bell Labs' first practical silicon cell

deep.x: Efficiency
Einstein's 1921 Nobel Prize was awarded for explaining the photoelectric effect, a related phenomenon, not for relativity.

cards.title: Células, paneles, strings
cards.text: Una célula produce unos 0,5–0,6 V. Decenas de células en serie forman un panel; varios paneles en serie forman un string de unos cientos de voltios que alimenta un inversor.

deep.x: Solar cells are combined into panels, and panels into strings, to reach useful voltages and powers.
Typical values
Half-cut cells
Many modern panels use cells cut in half, which reduces current per cell, lowers losses and improves shade tolerance.
Safety
DC strings carry high voltages whenever the sun shines and can't simply be "switched off" at the panels. Installation must follow strict rules.
Cells in series raise the voltage to something an inverter can use.

cards.title: Vatio pico
cards.text: Los paneles se clasifican en vatios pico (Wp): la potencia en condiciones estándar de prueba, con 1000 W/m² de luz solar a 25 °C. La producción real suele ser menor por el calor, el ángulo y el polvo.

deep.x: Panels are rated in watt-peak (Wp): their output under standard test conditions (STC). Real-world output is usually lower.
Why real output is lower
Typical performance

v.unit: output of a 400 Wp panel, W (approx.)

deep.x: Price trends
Solar module prices fell by roughly 90% between 2010 and 2020 and kept falling in the 2020s, making solar one of the cheapest sources of new electricity.
Wp is a lab rating; real panels rarely hit it.

cards.title: ¿Cuánto producirá?
example: Instalación de 4 kWp en el norte de Portugal (≈1400)
cards.text: En Portugal, cada kWp de paneles bien orientados suele producir unos 1400–1700 kWh al año, de lo mejor de Europa.

deep.x: In Portugal, each kilowatt-peak of well-oriented panels produces roughly 1,400–1,700 kWh a year, one of the best yields in Europe.
Regional yields
Example
That's more than a typical Portuguese household uses in a year, though production and use don't match in time.
Seasons

items.b: up to twice the winter output

deep.x: Portugal's sun makes each solar panel worth about 60% more than in Germany.

cards.title: Orientación e inclinación
cards.text: En Portugal, los paneles orientados al sur con unos 30–35° de inclinación dan la máxima energía a lo largo del año. Las disposiciones este–oeste producen menos en total, pero reparten la producción a lo largo del día.

deep.x: Panel orientation and tilt determine how much sunlight they capture over the year.
The optimum
In Portugal, south-facing panels tilted at roughly 30–35° collect the most energy over the year, close to the latitude minus a few degrees.
East–west layouts
Flat roofs
Panels on flat roofs are usually tilted on frames, or laid flatter in east–west rows to fit more panels on the roof.
South at 30–35° maximises energy; east–west better matches daily use.

cards.title: La sombra importa

steps: Ayudan optimizadores o diodos de bypass

cards.text: Una pequeña sombra sobre una célula puede reducir la producción de todo un string, porque las células en serie llevan la misma corriente. Los diodos de bypass y los optimizadores limitan el daño.

deep.x: Shading even a small part of a solar panel can reduce output disproportionately, because cells in series all carry the same current.
Bypass diodes
Panels contain bypass diodes, typically three per panel, that route current around shaded sections, limiting the loss to part of the panel.
Optimisers and microinverters

items: shade on one panel affects the string

deep.x: Hot spots
A shaded cell forced to carry current can heat up and be damaged. Persistent partial shading, such as from a chimney, should be avoided in design.
Check for chimneys, trees and antennas before deciding where panels go.

cards.title: El calor reduce la producción
cards.text: Las células de silicio pierden aproximadamente un 0,3–0,4 % de producción por cada °C por encima de 25 °C. En un tejado caluroso de verano, las células pueden llegar a 60 °C y perder más del 10 %.

deep.x: Solar cells work better when cool. Silicon panels lose about 0.3–0.4% of output for every °C above 25 °C.
Example
Cooling helps

x: Mounting with air gaps behind panels

deep.x: Best months
In Portugal, spring often gives excellent output: strong sun, long days and cooler temperatures than midsummer.
Floating solar farms on reservoirs, such as Alqueva's, benefit from water cooling, which slightly improves efficiency.

cards.title: Autoconsumo

items: Añade una batería para la noche

cards.text: La energía solar vale más cuando la usas mientras se produce, porque la que exportas se paga menos de lo que cuesta la que importas. Pon el lavavajillas, calienta agua o carga el coche a mediodía.

deep.x: Solar power is most valuable when used directly at home, because exported electricity earns much less than imported electricity costs.
The economics
In Portugal
Household systems operate under the self-consumption regime (UPAC). Surplus can be sold to a supplier, and renewable energy communities let neighbours share solar.
Batteries
Use solar when the sun shines; export only what you can't.

cards.title: Inversores
cards.text: Los inversores de string convierten la CC de los paneles en CA para la casa. Los inversores híbridos también pueden cargar y descargar una batería. Los microinversores van detrás de cada panel.

deep.x: Inverters convert DC from panels into AC for the home and grid. They also optimise panel output and monitor performance.
Hybrid inverters
A hybrid inverter connects panels, a battery and the grid, deciding where energy goes moment by moment.
Maximum power point tracking
Lifespan
The inverter is the brain of a solar system, and often the first part to replace.

cards.title: Amortización
cards.text: En un país soleado como Portugal, una instalación doméstica suele amortizarse en unos 5–8 años, según el precio, el autoconsumo y las tarifas. Los paneles suelen tener garantías de rendimiento de 25 años.

deep.x: In Portugal's sunny climate, home solar systems often pay back their cost in roughly 5–8 years, then produce cheap electricity for decades.
What drives payback
Example
Degradation
Panels lose about 0.3–0.5% of output per year. After 25 years, good panels still produce more than 80% of their original output.
Sun, self-consumption and price decide how fast solar pays back.

quiz.q: ¿Qué significa «Wp»?
options: Vatio pico: la potencia en condiciones estándar de prueba
quiz.explain: Se mide a 1000 W/m² y 25 °C.

quiz.q: ¿Hacia dónde deben orientarse los paneles en Portugal para obtener la máxima energía anual?
quiz.explain: El sol recorre el cielo por el sur.

quiz.q: ¿Por qué los paneles calientes producen menos?
options: Las células de silicio pierden eficiencia al subir la temperatura
quiz.explain: Alrededor de un 0,35 % por cada °C por encima de 25 °C.

lessons.title: Elegir cables
lessons.summary: Secciones, caída de tensión y por qué importa el tamaño.

cards.title: Los cables se calientan
cards.text: Todo cable tiene algo de resistencia, así que la corriente lo calienta (I² × R). Un cable demasiado fino para la corriente se sobrecalienta, daña su aislamiento y puede provocar un incendio.

deep.x: Every cable has resistance, so current through it produces heat. Size the cable correctly and the heat is harmless; undersize it and insulation degrades or melts.
Doubling the current
What limits current
Insulation ratings
A cable's capacity is really its ability to get rid of heat.

cards.title: Sección en mm²
cards.text: El tamaño de un cable es el área de cobre en milímetros cuadrados. Más área, menos resistencia y más corriente puede llevar con seguridad.

deep.x: Cable size is given by the copper cross-sectional area in square millimetres. Larger area means lower resistance and more current capacity.
Resistance per metre
Diameter vs area
Area grows with the square of diameter: a 6 mm² conductor has four times the area of 1.5 mm², but only twice the diameter.
Not AWG
North America uses AWG gauge numbers, where bigger numbers mean thinner wires. Europe uses mm² directly.
Capacities depend on installation: always use the official tables.

cards.title: Secciones típicas en casa
cards.text: Práctica habitual en Portugal: 1,5 mm² para alumbrado, 2,5 mm² para enchufes, 4 mm² para hornos o termos, 6 mm² para un cargador de VE o una bomba de calor grande. Comprueba siempre la normativa de instalación y el cálculo del instalador.

deep.x: Typical residential practice in Portugal follows the RTIEBT technical rules. Sizes depend on load, length and installation method, so installers must calculate.
Supply cable
The cable from the meter to the board is sized for the contracted power, often 10 mm² or larger for single phase.
Long runs

x: 40 m run to a garden studio at 16 A

deep.x: Certification
New installations in Portugal require a project or declaration by a qualified electrician and inspection by an authorised body before connection.
Typical sizes are a starting point; the calculation decides.

cards.title: El automático protege el cable

items.w: el automático de 16 A salta a menudo
items.r: busca la sobrecarga
recablear con cable más grueso si hace falta

cards.text: El automático debe tener un calibre tal que el cable nunca lleve más corriente de la que soporta con seguridad. Cambiar un automático de 16 A por uno de 25 A «porque salta mucho» elimina la protección.

deep.x: A breaker's rating must never exceed what the cable can safely carry. Its job is to trip before the cable overheats.

items.w: Breaker keeps tripping, fit a bigger one
items.r: Find the cause: overload or fault

deep.x: Matching
Why upsizing is dangerous
Real causes of tripping

items: Too many appliances on one circuit

deep.x: If a breaker trips, it's doing its job: listen to it.

cards.title: Caída de tensión
cards.text: Los cables largos pierden tensión por el camino. La normativa suele limitar la caída a un pequeño porcentaje. En monofásica, la caída es aproximadamente dos veces la longitud por la corriente por la resistencia por metro.

deep.x: Long cables lose voltage along their length. Too much drop makes motors struggle, lights dim and electronics misbehave.
Example
Limits
Fixes
For long runs, voltage drop often decides the cable size, not heat.

cards.title: El método de instalación importa
cards.text: Un cable enterrado en aislante o agrupado con otros no puede disipar el calor, así que lleva con seguridad menos corriente que uno al aire libre.

deep.x: How a cable is installed affects how well it sheds heat, and therefore how much current it can safely carry.

v.unit: relative capacity of the same cable, % (illustrative)

deep.x: Derating
Cable tables give base capacities, then correction factors for grouping, ambient temperature and thermal insulation.
Hot spots

x: Bundles of many circuits in one trunking
Cables near hot water pipes or in sunny areas

deep.x: Planning
The same cable can be safe in air and overheated in insulation.

cards.title: Colores
cards.text: En Europa: el marrón es la fase, el azul es el neutro y el verde y amarillo es la tierra de protección. Las instalaciones portuguesas antiguas pueden usar otros colores, así que nunca te fíes solo de los colores.

deep.x: Conductor colours help identify their function. In Europe, harmonised colours have been standard for decades, but older installations may differ.
Never trust colours alone
Older or altered installations may use non-standard colours, and DIY work can swap them. Always test before touching.
Green-yellow is only for earth
The green-and-yellow conductor must never be used for anything other than protective earth.
Colours are a guide, not a guarantee.

cards.title: Flexible frente a rígido
cards.text: La instalación fija usa conductores rígidos, de un solo hilo o de varios. Los cables de los aparatos y los alargadores usan cable flexible de muchos hilos que aguanta que lo dobles.

deep.x: Cables are built differently depending on whether they stay fixed or move.
Using the wrong one

x: Rigid cable in a moving application cracks over time
Flexible strands need ferrules in screw terminals to avoid loose strands

deep.x: Common types in Portugal
Outdoors
Outdoor cables need UV-resistant, waterproof sheaths, and buried cables need protection or armouring.
Fixed wiring stays rigid; anything that moves must be flexible.

cards.title: Alargadores

items: Mira los vatios máx. en la etiqueta

cards.text: Un alargador de carrete debe desenrollarse del todo para cargas altas; si no, el cable enrollado atrapa el calor y puede fundirse. Nunca encadenes regletas para calefactores o hervidores.

deep.x: Extension leads are convenient but often misused. Many electrical fires start with overloaded or damaged extensions.
Reels
A coiled reel traps heat; most have two ratings printed on them.
Multi-plug adapters
Plugging a heater, kettle and toaster into one adapter can exceed 16 A, overheating the adapter and the socket.
Warning signs
High-power appliances belong in wall sockets, not on extensions.

cards.title: Aluminio frente a cobre
cards.text: El aluminio conduce aproximadamente un 60 % de lo que conduce el cobre, así que necesita más sección, pero es más ligero y barato. Las líneas aéreas usan aluminio; la instalación de las casas, cobre.

deep.x: Copper and aluminium are the main conductor metals. Each has its uses.
Weight advantage
For the same resistance, an aluminium conductor weighs about half as much as copper, which is why overhead lines use aluminium, often reinforced with a steel core.
Problems in homes
Aluminium wiring in some 1960s–70s homes in North America caused connection fires; special connectors are needed.
Today
