quiz.explain: Almacena lo que, si no, comprarías tras la puesta de sol.

quiz.q: ¿Dónde debe funcionar un generador de gasolina?
options: Al aire libre, lejos de las ventanas
quiz.explain: El monóxido de carbono es mortal.

lessons.title: Una historia de la electricidad
lessons.summary: Del ámbar a la red inteligente.

cards.title: El ámbar y la palabra «eléctrico»
cards.text: Los antiguos griegos observaron que el ámbar frotado atraía plumas. La palabra griega para el ámbar, «elektron», nos dio «electricidad», un término acuñado por William Gilbert hacia 1600.

deep.x: Electricity's name comes from amber. Ancient Greeks noticed that rubbed amber attracted light objects like feathers and straw.
Gilbert's work
English physician William Gilbert's 1600 book "De Magnete" studied magnetism and static electricity, coining the Latin word "electricus" (amber-like) for materials that attract when rubbed.
Elektron

items.b: first used in English by Thomas Browne, 1646

deep.x: Early experiments
Electricity is named after a fossilised tree resin.

cards.title: La pila de Volta, 1800
cards.text: Alessandro Volta apiló discos de zinc y cobre separados por paños empapados en salmuera: la primera pila que daba una corriente estable. El voltio lleva su nombre.

deep.x: Alessandro Volta's "voltaic pile" was the first source of steady electric current, opening the door to modern electrical science.
The frog debate
Luigi Galvani had observed frog legs twitching with metals and believed in "animal electricity". Volta argued the metals generated the electricity and built the pile to prove it.
Consequences
Humphry Davy used powerful batteries to isolate sodium and potassium in 1807.
Honour
The volt is named after Volta. Napoleon made him a count in recognition of his work.
The battery turned electricity from sparks into a steady flow.

cards.title: Los descubrimientos de Faraday
cards.text: En 1831, Michael Faraday demostró que los imanes en movimiento inducen corrientes, la base de todo generador y transformador. Apenas tuvo educación formal y se convirtió en uno de los mayores experimentadores de la historia.

deep.x: Michael Faraday, largely self-taught, made some of the most important discoveries in electrical science.

items.l: born to a blacksmith's family in London

deep.x: From apprentice to scientist
Faraday left school early and became a bookbinder's apprentice, reading the books he bound. He attended Humphry Davy's lectures and became his assistant at the Royal Institution.
His legacy
The farad
The unit of capacitance, the farad, honours him.
Faraday started the Royal Institution's Christmas Lectures for young people in 1825; they continue today.

cards.title: Las ecuaciones de Maxwell
cards.text: En la década de 1860, James Clerk Maxwell escribió cuatro ecuaciones que unificaban la electricidad, el magnetismo y la luz. Predijeron las ondas de radio, que Hertz demostró en 1887.

deep.x: In the 1860s, James Clerk Maxwell described electricity, magnetism and light in one theory. It remains one of the greatest achievements in physics.
The prediction
Maxwell's equations showed that changing electric and magnetic fields create waves travelling at the speed of light, so light itself must be an electromagnetic wave.
The four equations in words

items.b: magnetic field lines have no start or end
changing magnetic fields create electric fields
currents and changing electric fields create magnetic fields

deep.x: Impact
Maxwell revealed that light is electricity and magnetism dancing together.

cards.title: Las bombillas

events.l: central de Pearl Street, Nueva York
electrificación general de hogares en EE. UU.

cards.text: Muchos inventores trabajaron en la luz eléctrica. En 1879, Edison y, en Gran Bretaña, Swan produjeron bombillas prácticas y duraderas de filamento de carbono. Edison también construyó las centrales y la red para vender electricidad.

deep.x: Electric light transformed daily life. Many inventors contributed, but Edison and Swan produced the first practical long-lasting bulbs around 1879.
Edison's system
Edison's genius was not only the bulb but the whole system: generators, wiring, meters and fuses. His Pearl Street station in New York opened in 1882.
Ediswan
After a patent dispute in Britain, Edison and Swan merged their British companies in 1883 as "Ediswan".
From filaments to LEDs
Nobel Prize
Isamu Akasaki, Hiroshi Amano and Shuji Nakamura received the 2014 Nobel Prize in Physics for blue LEDs, which made white LED lighting possible.
The light bulb needed a whole electrical system to shine.

cards.title: La electricidad en Portugal
cards.text: Las primeras luces eléctricas de Portugal se encendieron en Cascais en 1878. Las grandes presas hidroeléctricas construidas desde la década de 1950 en ríos como el Zêzere y el Duero impulsaron la electrificación del país.

deep.x: Electricity reached Portugal in the late 19th century, and hydropower drove electrification across the 20th century.

events.l: Central Tejo power station in Lisbon

deep.x: Central Tejo
Lisbon's Central Tejo power station, built in stages from 1909, supplied much of the city's electricity until the 1970s. It's now part of the MAAT museum in Belém.
Hydro era

items: Castelo do Bode on the Zêzere

deep.x: No nuclear
Portugal never built a nuclear power plant. A project at Ferrel, near Peniche, was abandoned in the 1970s after local protests.
Modern era
Portugal electrified with water, then wind and sun.

cards.title: El transistor, 1947

steps: Miles de millones por chip hoy

cards.text: En los Bell Labs, Bardeen, Brattain y Shockley construyeron el primer transistor. Sustituyó a las voluminosas válvulas de vacío e hizo posibles la electrónica moderna, los ordenadores y los móviles.

deep.x: The transistor, invented at Bell Labs in December 1947, is the foundation of all modern electronics.
The inventors
John Bardeen, Walter Brattain and William Shockley shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics for the transistor.
Scale
What a transistor does

items.b: small signal controls a larger one

deep.x: Billions of tiny switches now fit on a fingernail-sized chip.

cards.title: Nuclear y renovables

events.l: las renovables lideran la nueva potencia

cards.text: Las primeras centrales nucleares aparecieron en la década de 1950. Desde los años 2000, la eólica y después la solar crecieron rápidamente a medida que bajaban los costes; el precio de los módulos solares cayó alrededor de un 90 % en la década de 2010.

deep.x: The second half of the 20th century brought nuclear power; the 21st brought the rapid rise of wind and solar.
Falling costs
Nuclear today
Nuclear provides around a tenth of the world's electricity, with low carbon emissions but high construction costs and long build times.
Renewables today
Wind and solar are now the cheapest sources of new electricity in many countries, and their share grows every year.
Renewables went from expensive niche to cheapest option in about a decade.

cards.title: Unidades con nombre de persona
cards.text: Muchas unidades honran a científicos: voltio (Volta), amperio (Ampère), ohmio (Ohm), vatio (Watt), hercio (Hertz), culombio (Coulomb), tesla (Tesla).

deep.x: Most electrical units honour scientists who made key discoveries.
More units
Writing rules

items.r: 230 volts (230 V), 10 amps (10 A)

deep.x: Unit names are lowercase when written out; symbols for units named after people are capitalised.
James Watt worked on steam engines, not electricity, but his name became the universal unit of power.

cards.title: Lo que viene
cards.text: La electricidad está asumiendo una parte cada vez mayor del uso de energía: coches, calefacción, industria. Los retos ahora son el almacenamiento, la ampliación de la red y casar la oferta renovable variable con la demanda.

deep.x: Electricity is taking over more of the energy system. The challenges now are storage, grids and flexibility.
Electrification

items.l: electricity's share of global final energy
as cars, heating and industry electrify

deep.x: Challenges
Data centres and AI
Rapid growth of data centres, driven partly by AI, is increasing electricity demand in several countries, including new projects in Portugal such as at Sines.
The future of energy is increasingly electric.
